title: Intrinsic varying-ring clopen proper/open arrows
statement: Use the ordinary and derived varying-ring operations and their canonical compositors [def-sp-varying-ring-operations]. For a commutative scheme square $k:V\to W$, $r:V\to S$, $p:W\to T$, $i:S\to T$ with $k,i$ quasi-compact open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] and $p,r$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], form $W'=W\times_T S$ [def-pc-fibre-product], $b:W'\to W$, $q:W'\to S$ and the canonical lift $s=(k,r)$. It is open and closed [def-weil-closed-immersion] by the geometric assertion of [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus]. For a cartesian open square define $\beta^{-1}:j'_!g_U^*\to g^*j_!$ as the open-adjunction transpose of inverse-image composition after the open unit. This is invertible; let $\beta$ be its inverse. The open unit is invertible, and its inverse's mate defines $j_!\to j_*$. For clopen $s$ this map is invertible; define $\pi_s:\mathrm{id}\to s_!s^*$ as the $s^*\dashv s_*$ unit followed by its inverse. Define the ordinary system transformation $a_Q:p^*i_!\to k_!r^*$ as $\beta$, followed by $b_!\pi_s q^*$ and the canonical open and inverse-image compositors. Localize this actual system transformation to obtain $a_Q$ on ordinary unbounded derived categories. Define $\gamma_Q:i_!Rr_*\to Rp_*k_!$ to be its mate under $r^*\dashv Rr_*$ and $p^*\dashv Rp_*$, namely the unit--$a_Q$--counit composite. For comparison with a single arbitrary constant ring $B$, use the exact diagonal of [lem-sf-cbc-constant-tower-direct-image-normalization] to embed a coefficient complex as a constant strict tower and evaluate at $0$ the strict-tower clopen mate from [lem-cbc-strict-tower-proper-open-calculus], transporting by its canonical evaluation maps and the constant-tower evaluation isomorphism. This defines the normalized single-coefficient mate also for infinite rings.

proof.text: Construct the inverse-image square isomorphism by the two moduleGComp compositors and equality transport. Its equality to this formula uniquely determines it; choose from that proved unique specification so the kernel need not unfold the adjoint-compositor expression in subsequent naturality checks. moduleSquareG_eq recovers the original formula.

For moduleBetaInvApp_naturality apply naturality of the inverse open-adjunction Hom equivalence. Naturality of the open unit rewrites the initial pullback map, and naturality of the inverse square isomorphism identifies the remaining composites.
For moduleJ_congr substitute equality of the scheme maps. Proof irrelevance identifies the open-immersion instances, and the extension functors are reflexively equal.

Recover the single-coefficient derived open-unit isomorphism by embedding a complex as a constant strict tower, using strict-tower evaluation for J and G, inverting the strict open unit, and evaluating back. An isomorphism JG ≅ id implies that the specified level open unit is invertible. The inverse-mate unit identity for evalJInv and joint detection by coefficient evaluations then make the varying-ring derived open unit invertible. Apply degree-zero single-complex homology to obtain an isomorphism of the ordinary composite with the identity; adjunction rigidity makes moduleJAdj.unit invertible.

For a cartesian open square, the existing arbitrary-ring strict-tower beta, constant embedding and evaluation give a single-coefficient isomorphism g* j! M ≅ j'! a* M. Thus evaluation of G_g J_j M belongs to the essential image of the fully faithful level open extension. The level open counit there is invertible. The inverse-mate counit identity for evalJInv, followed by joint detection, proves invertibility of the varying derived open counit at G_g J_j M. On degree-zero single complexes, homology gives ordinary essential-image membership of g* j! M. The ordinary open counit is therefore invertible. In moduleBetaInvApp its transpose is a composite of the pullback of an invertible open unit and the inverse square isomorphism. Expanding the Hom inverse as extension of the transpose followed by counit proves moduleBetaInv_isIso componentwise.

For a clopen immersion recover a single-level derived isomorphism J ≅ P from the strict-tower openToR isomorphism by constant embedding and evaluation. The fully faithful level J transfers full faithfulness to P, so its pullback/direct-image unit is invertible on evaluated J objects. The evalPMate unit identity and joint detection make the varying derived unit invertible on J objects. This unit and the inverse open unit construct a varying derived isomorphism J ≅ P. Taking degree-zero homology on single complexes, using the natural identification H⁰(RP(M[0])) ≅ R⁰P(M) ≅ P(M), gives an ordinary isomorphism extension ≅ push. Full faithfulness transfers from extension to push; the ordinary direct-image unit is invertible on extension objects. Each component of the specified moduleOpenToP is this unit followed by push of the inverse open unit, hence is invertible.

proof_origin.place: Tags 03DI, 07A7 and 09AE; existing arbitrary-ring strict-tower invertibility transported by constant embedding and canonical coefficient evaluation. The proof uses unit/counit mate identities only to detect isomorphisms, not equality of arbitrary derived morphisms. Degree-zero homology recovers the ordinary statements.
